reports.text:
Indication: jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, elevated transaminases.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the right upper quadrant.
Liver: normal in size and echotexture. No focal hepatic lesion.
Biliary: no intrahepatic or extrahepatic ductal dilatation. Common bile duct 3 mm.
Gallbladder: normally distended, no stones, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy sign negative.
Portal vein: patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Pancreas: visualized portions unremarkable.
Right kidney: normal size, no hydronephrosis.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal right upper quadrant ultrasound. No biliary obstruction.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital, Emergency Department. Date of visit 06/19/2026, arrived 18:50, discharged 23:40. Faxed to primary care 07/10/2026 on request.

CHIEF COMPLAINT: feeling unwell x1 week, urine dark.

HPI: 35M, generally healthy, about a week of malaise and tiredness. Noticed his urine turning dark, "like tea," over the same week. Some mild nausea, has not vomited. Denies abdominal pain. No fever he has measured. Got back from a work trip to Southeast Asia earlier this month. History of remote IV drug use, none currently. Had hepatitis at 24 which resolved on its own. No acetaminophen beyond a couple of doses, no supplements or herbal products, no new medications.

PMH: IVDU, in remission. Hepatitis age 24, resolved.
MEDS: none.
ALLERGIES: NKDA.
FAMILY HX: father with alcohol use disorder; mother with HTN.
SOCIAL: never smoker. EtOH socially, 1 to 2 per week. International logistics consultant.

ROS: positive as in HPI. Negative for chest pain, SOB, confusion, bleeding or bruising, rash.

EXAM: T 37.3, HR 88, BP 128/78, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA.
Gen: tired-appearing, nontoxic, alert and oriented.
Eyes: sclerae mildly icteric.
CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nondistended, tender to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Liver not enlarged. No splenomegaly. No ascites.
Skin: no rash, no petechiae, no spider angiomata.
Neuro: nonfocal, no asterixis.

RESULTS:
AST 980 U/L, ALT 1150 U/L, total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, alk phos 110 U/L, albumin 4.2 g/dL. INR 1.0. Remainder of CMP and CBC unremarkable.
RUQ US: normal liver, no biliary dilatation, gallbladder normal.
Acute hepatitis panel sent, pending at discharge.

MDM: marked hepatocellular transaminase elevation with mild hyperbilirubinemia, preserved synthetic function (normal INR and albumin), normal mental status, imaging without obstruction. Picture is acute hepatitis, most likely viral given recent travel. Tolerating PO. No indication for admission.

DIAGNOSIS: acute hepatitis, likely viral.

DISPOSITION: home. Avoid alcohol. Limit acetaminophen. Hydrate. Follow up with PCP in 2 to 3 days for repeat labs and serology results. Return for confusion, vomiting and unable to keep fluids down, bleeding, worsening yellowing or abdominal pain.

Electronically signed, ED attending physician.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to give you a heads up. I've felt run down for about a week and my pee got really dark so I went to the ER last night. They said my liver numbers were way up and it's probably a virus, maybe from my trip, and to see you in a couple days. They did an ultrasound which was fine. They sent some hepatitis tests but those weren't back when I left. I still feel crummy but ok, eating a little. When can you see me?

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, Austin, and sorry you're feeling lousy. I can see you Monday or Tuesday morning, whichever is easier. Until then: no alcohol, no more than a couple of Tylenol a day if any, keep drinking fluids. If you get confused or very sleepy, can't keep anything down, notice bleeding or bruising, or the yellow color gets worse, go back to the ER. I'll ask the hospital for the records.

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen Friday night in the ED for about a week of malaise, fatigue and dark urine. ED records not here yet; requested today. History from him.

He got back in early June from roughly three weeks working in Southeast Asia, client sites and a lot of meals out. Started feeling off around the 12th: tired, no appetite, queasy, then dark urine. ED told him his liver enzymes were very high, ultrasound normal, hepatitis tests sent. Since then about the same, maybe slightly better today. Mild nausea, no vomiting. No abdominal pain to speak of. No fever. Stools normal color. No itching, no confusion, no bleeding or bruising. Took two Tylenol total last week, nothing since. No supplements. No alcohol since before the trip ended. No IV drug use. NKDA, no meds.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, afebrile. Weight 76 kg, about 3 kg below December. Tired but comfortable, fully alert and conversant. Sclerae mildly icteric. Skin without jaundice of note, no excoriations, no bruises, no spider angiomata. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender in the RUQ, liver edge not palpable, no splenomegaly, no ascites. No asterixis.

Assessment: acute hepatitis, presumed viral, after travel to an area where hepatitis A is common. Hepatitis B unlikely given his immune serology last year. Checking synthetic function today.

Plan:
- CMP, PT/INR, CBC, acute hepatitis panel (HAV IgM, HBsAg, HBc IgM, HCV Ab).
- Supportive care. No alcohol until liver tests normal. Acetaminophen 2 g/day max. Small frequent meals, fluids.
- Out of work through 7/6, letter given; no travel for now.
- Reviewed warning signs that need same-day call or ED.
- Will call with results. Recheck in about 2 weeks.
- ED record request faxed with his signed release.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Austin Morin was seen in this office today and is under my care for a medical illness. He is unable to work from 6/19/2026 through 7/6/2026 and should not travel during this time. I expect him to be able to return after that; I will update this note if anything changes.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Results call: acute hepatitis A
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Hepatitis A IgM reactive: acute hepatitis A. HBsAg and HBc IgM nonreactive, HCV Ab nonreactive. Yesterday's labs: AST 412, ALT 688, T bili 2.7, ALP 121, albumin 4.0, INR 1.0, CBC normal. Liver is making its proteins normally.

Explained: likely picked up through food or water on the trip, usually clears completely in weeks to a couple of months, no chronic form, and afterward he is immune for life. Contagious mainly before and in the first week or so of jaundice: careful handwashing, don't prepare food for others for now. Lives alone; nobody else at home. Not a food handler. Reportable, so the health department may call him.

Same precautions: no alcohol, acetaminophen limit. Recheck visit 7/8 with labs. He was relieved to have an answer.

documents.title: Call from public health nurse
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Public health nurse from the local health department called regarding the reportable hepatitis A result on this patient. Confirmed the lab, collection date 6/23, and symptom onset about 6/12. Provided travel history as documented. Confirmed he is not a food handler or health care worker. She has already spoken with the patient and is handling contact follow-up on their end. No action needed from us. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Records request and check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Still no ED records from the 6/19 visit. Called the hospital's health information office; they have our 6/23 request logged but nothing went out. Re-faxed the request and signed release, they say 3 to 5 business days.

Also called pt to check in before his Wednesday visit. Says energy is noticeably better, eating normally again, urine back to normal color, eyes look less yellow. No nausea. Working a little from home. Reminded him of labs at the visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: acute hepatitis A
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of acute hepatitis A (HAV IgM reactive 6/24, onset ~6/12 after travel).

Much improved. Energy perhaps 80 percent of normal, appetite back, nausea gone. Urine normal color for about a week. Stools normal. No abdominal pain, no itching. Still no alcohol. No acetaminophen. Has been working half days from home since last week and wants to go back fully. Has a client trip abroad penciled in for late August and asks if that's realistic.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, afebrile. Weight 77 kg, up 1 kg. Sclerae anicteric today. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly. No asterixis.

A/P: acute hepatitis A, resolving as expected.
- Hepatic panel today.
- OK to return to work, remote or in the office, now. Hold on international travel until liver tests are normal.
- Continue no alcohol until normal.
- Repeat hepatic panel in 3 weeks, then again if not normal. No visit needed if trending down.
- ED records still outstanding; RN re-requested Monday.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Austin: your liver tests have come down a lot. ALT is now 214 (it was 688 two weeks ago) and bilirubin 1.3, close to normal. Albumin is normal. This is exactly the direction we want. Next blood draw around July 29; you can just come in for the lab, no appointment with me needed.

documents.title: ED record received and reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED record from 6/19 finally received by fax (second request): provider note, labs and RUQ ultrasound report. Reviewed.

At the ED: AST 980, ALT 1150, T bili 3.2, ALP 110, albumin 4.2, INR 1.0, CBC normal. RUQ US normal liver, no ductal dilatation, normal gallbladder. Exam with mild scleral icterus and RUQ tenderness, no enlarged liver. Discharged home with dx acute hepatitis, likely viral. The ED's own hepatitis panel is listed as pending; no result included in what they sent.

Consistent with what he told us and with our 6/23 and 7/8 labs showing steady improvement. Nothing new to act on.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Austin, almost there. Bilirubin is normal now (0.8) and AST is normal. ALT is 61, still a bit above the normal range but way down from where it was. One more check in about 3 weeks, mid-August. If that's normal you're cleared for the trip and for a drink again.

documents.title: RE: Liver tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, feeling basically normal now. I'll come in Monday the 17th first thing. The trip is the last week of August so that timing works if it's good.

documents.title: Liver tests normal
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Austin, yesterday's liver tests are completely normal: ALT 27, AST 23, bilirubin 0.6. The hepatitis A is over. You're cleared to travel and back to your usual drinking is fine. You now have lifelong immunity to hepatitis A, so you won't need the vaccine. No more blood tests for this. See you for your physical in December.

documents.title: RE: Liver tests normal
documents.author: patient
documents.body: That's a relief, thanks for staying on top of it. Weight's back to about 78 too. See you in December.
